text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they often add it to a shared project. A CI system then automatically starts an automated build to check that everything still works. During this process, it also runs tests to make sure the new code does not break anything. The main goal is catching issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines usually include several steps, such as building, testing, and reporting results. This helps teams work faster and with more confidence.
